subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on BMW engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the S65 across all 1 model applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The S65 is a single-application engine — the E9X M3 across all four body styles.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Bearings, gaskets and seals as standard on every rebuild, with timing chain components replaced where required. Throttle actuators and VANOS components are inspected and measured as part of every rebuild.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: Rod bearing wear and throttle actuator failure are the documented patterns for the S65 — these are established in the BMW M specialist community and we inspect both as part of every rebuild. We don't treat this engine as having a universal failure mode beyond that; diagnosis is required to establish whether an individual engine needs repair, rebuild or replacement.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page - they'll be added once a documented set of completed S65 rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.
